text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

VEGOIL SALE - Egypt's official Holding Company for Food Industries bought 28,500 tonnes of sunflower oil at $560 per tonne for delivery in the second half of August. Egypt scrapped its tenders for cottonseed oil and soybean oil due to high prices. The firm had originally tendered for 25,000 to 40,000 tonnes of cottonseed, sunflower and soybean oils.
WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan would be seeking on July 28 a total of 500,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for August 11 to September 10 shipment, a Pakistan embassy official said.

WHEAT TENDERS cont'd - The CCC said it was seeking up to 6,360 tonnes of U.S. no. 2 or better hard red winter wheat for donation to Tunisia. The shipment period was slated for August 10-August 31. Offers were due on July 22.

- Algeria has launched a tender for the import of 75,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat for September shipment, European grain traders said. Exporters also said Algeria was seeking 150,000 tonnes of durum wheat for shipment in August and September. Results of both tenders were due later this week.

WHEAT TENDER - Jordan is scheduled to tender July 23 for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter or hard red spring wheat or equivalent wheat from other countries, U.S. exporters said. Half of the tonnage was slated for last-half August shipment and the balance for last-half September shipment.

CORN/SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company was seeking 30,000 tonnes of U.S. or Argentine No. 2 yellow corn for arrival in the second half of September and/or the second half of October and 30,000 tonnes of soybean, any origin, for arrival first half of October and/or first half of November. The deadline for bids is noon is July 22.

RICE TENDERS - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs will receive offers until July 23 to buy 24,000 tonnes of white rice for August delivery, a GEZA spokesman said. Results would be available on July 24.
The CCC said it was seeking a total of 1,780 tonnes U.S. long grain rice on July 22 for donation to Burkina Faso. The shipment period was due for August 21 to September 5.

MARKET TALK - USDA officials have floated a plan that would allow them to replenish two emergency commodity reserves by taking money from the United States' main agricultural export subsidy and food aid programs. "I don't think at this point it's a formal proposal," according to one Senate aide briefed by USDA officials on the plan. "It's just something that people are kicking around."

... The United States accused North Korea on Wednesday of unusually aggressive provocation in sending soldiers across the demilitarized zone with South Korea but said it would not affect promised new food aid. The United States announced earlier this week that it was more than doubling its food aid from $25 million to $52 million to meet North Korea's famine.
